entities.name: Acharya Ramadev
entities.intro: A forceful professor at the Gurukul at Kangri.

entities.name: Sacred thread & shikha
entities.intro: The outward marks of a Hindu: the sacred thread worn by the upper castes, and the tuft of hair on the crown.

entities.name: Satyagraha Ashram
entities.intro: Gandhi's community in Ahmedabad, founded on 25 May 1915.

entities.name: Ahmedabad
entities.intro: Capital of Gujarat and an ancient centre of handloom weaving; a city of mills and wealthy merchants.

entities.name: Amritlal Thakkar (Thakkar Bapa)
entities.intro: A social worker devoted to the 'untouchable' and tribal communities.

entities.name: Dudabhai, Danibehn & Lakshmi
entities.intro: An 'untouchable' family: Dudabhai, a former teacher in Bombay, his wife Danibehn and their baby daughter Lakshmi.

entities.name: Champaran
entities.intro: A district of north Bihar near Nepal, where peasants were forced to grow indigo for European planters.

entities.name: Rajkumar Shukla
entities.intro: A simple, determined Champaran peasant who had suffered under the indigo system.

entities.name: Brajkishore Prasad
entities.intro: A Bihar vakil who took up poor tenants' cases.

entities.name: Rajendra Prasad
entities.intro: A Bihar lawyer, then away from Patna.

entities.name: Maulana Mazharul Haq
entities.intro: A Bihar leader and former London law student, president of the Muslim League in 1915.

entities.name: J. B. Kripalani
entities.intro: A Sindhi professor who had just resigned from the Government College in Muzaffarpur.

entities.name: Indigo & tinkathia
entities.intro: The 'tinkathia' system, under which Champaran tenants had to grow indigo on three-twentieths of their land for the planters.

entities.name: Civil disobedience
entities.intro: Openly disobeying an unjust order and accepting the penalty.

entities.name: Dr. Dev
entities.intro: A doctor of the Servants of India Society.

entities.name: Avantikabai Gokhale
entities.intro: A volunteer teacher from Bombay.

entities.name: Narahari Parikh
entities.intro: A young Gujarati who joined Gandhi with his wife Manibehn.

entities.name: Babasaheb Soman
entities.intro: A volunteer teacher sent by Gangadharrao Deshpande.

entities.name: Sir Edward Gait
entities.intro: Lieutenant Governor of Bihar.

entities.name: Anasuyabai Sarabhai
entities.intro: A labour organizer in Ahmedabad and sister of the mill-owner Ambalal Sarabhai.

entities.name: Ambalal Sarabhai
entities.intro: A leading Ahmedabad mill-owner and Anasuyabai's brother.

entities.name: Vallabhbhai Patel
entities.intro: An Ahmedabad barrister.

entities.name: Shankarlal Banker
entities.intro: An Ahmedabad public worker.

entities.name: Ahmedabad mill strike
entities.intro: The 1918 strike by Ahmedabad textile workers for higher wages.

entities.name: Kheda

entities.intro: Gandhi's ideas on care for cattle.

chapters.situation: After the noisy Kumbha fair at Hardvar, Gandhi goes on to Swami Shraddhanand's Gurukul and the pilgrim sites upriver.
chapters.summary: At the peaceful Gurukul Gandhi argues for industrial training with Acharya Ramadev. At Rishikesh a sannyasi is pained that Gandhi wears neither the sacred thread nor the shikha. Gandhi explains he will not wear a thread denied to Shudras, and that Hindus have no right to such a symbol until Hinduism purges itself of untouchability. He admits he cut his shikha out of shame before going to England, even making Chhaganlal cut his, and decides to regrow it. He finds the Lakshman Jhula iron bridge ugly and the riverbanks fouled.

updates.gandhi: Refuses the sacred thread but regrows his shikha, which he had cut off out of shame before going to England.
updates.shraddhanand: Welcomes Gandhi warmly to the peaceful Gurukul.
updates.ramadev: Becomes a friend despite their differences; they discuss industrial training.
updates.chhaganlal: Gandhi had made him cut his shikha in South Africa and now regrets it.
updates.sacredthread: The thread should be refused while Shudras are denied it and untouchability remains. The shikha is regrown.
updates.untouchability: Gandhi links the right to wear Hindu symbols to purging untouchability.
updates.hardvar: Pilgrims foul the beautiful banks of the Ganges, and the iron bridge spoils the scene.
updates.sanitation: People relieve themselves on the sacred riverbanks.

chapters.situation: After the Kumbha and Hardvar, Gandhi must decide where to settle in India with his Phoenix family.
chapters.summary: Offered places in Hardvar, Vaidyanathadham and Rajkot, Gandhi chooses Ahmedabad. As a Gujarati he can best serve through his own language, the city is an ancient weaving centre suited to reviving hand-spinning, and its wealthy can help. He warns supporters he will admit any worthy untouchable. The Satyagraha Ashram opens on 25 May 1915 in Jivanlal Desai's Kochrab bungalow with about 25 men and women, 13 of them Tamils. A suggestion to add 'humility' as a vow is rejected on the grounds that humility that is vowed stops being humility.

updates.gandhi: Founds the Satyagraha Ashram at Kochrab, Ahmedabad, on 25 May 1915.
updates.shraddhanand: Wanted Gandhi to settle at Hardvar.
updates.ashram: Founded 25 May 1915 with about 25 people sharing a common kitchen. Named for both its goal and its method: truth and insistence on truth.
updates.ahmedabad: Chosen for its weaving heritage, its Gujarati language, and its wealthy patrons.
updates.untouchability: Gandhi declares from the start that the Ashram will admit untouchables.
updates.tamil: Thirteen Tamils are among the first ashram members, five of them from South Africa.
updates.satyagraha: Gandhi wants to test in India the method he tried in South Africa.

chapters.situation: The Satyagraha Ashram is only months old, and Gandhi has promised to admit untouchables.
chapters.summary: Amritlal Thakkar recommends an untouchable family, Dudabhai, Danibehn and baby Lakshmi, and the ashram admits them. The man at the well curses them for 'pollution' until their silence shames him. Donors stop all funding and a boycott is threatened. When Maganlal reports there is no money for next month, Gandhi says they will move to the untouchables' quarter. Then an unknown Sheth drives up and hands over Rs. 13,000 without coming in. Inside the ashram, Kasturba and other women show distaste for Danibehn, which troubles Gandhi more than the money.

updates.gandhi: Admits an untouchable family and is ready to move to the untouchables' quarter rather than give in.
updates.kasturba: Among the women who show indifference or dislike toward Danibehn, which pains Gandhi deeply.
updates.maganlal: Tells Gandhi the ashram has no money for the next month.
updates.thakkar: Recommends the untouchable family to the ashram.
updates.dudabhai: Admitted to the ashram. He bears insults patiently and persuades his wife to do the same.
updates.ashram: Loses its donors over the untouchable family, then is saved by an anonymous Rs. 13,000.
updates.untouchability: The ashram's first test. Gandhi notes that orthodox Hindus later fund an ashram that dines with untouchables.

chapters.situation: Gandhi's ashram has weathered the storm over admitting an untouchable family. Indentured emigration from India still goes on, though the Natal £3 tax ended in 1914.
chapters.summary: After Malaviya's resolution, the Viceroy promises only 'eventual' abolition of indenture. Gandhi pushes for a definite deadline of 31 July 1917, arguing people cannot act on a vague word like 'immediate'. He tours India alone in third class, followed by detectives and once shoved through a train window to stand all night. Before 31 July the government announces the end of indentured emigration, which Gandhi credits partly to 'potential satyagraha'.

updates.gandhi: Leads a nationwide campaign that ends indentured emigration in 1917. Travels alone, is shadowed by detectives, and is mistaken for a sadhu.
updates.malaviya: Moves resolutions to abolish the indenture system.
updates.hardinge: Promises only the eventual abolition of indenture.
updates.chelmsford: Refuses Malaviya's bill but promises Gandhi to be helpful.
updates.indenture: Indentured emigration ends before 31 July 1917. The £3 tax had ended with the Smuts-Gandhi Settlement of 1914.
updates.satyagraha: Gandhi says 'potential satyagraha' hastened the end of indenture.
updates.thirdclass: Shoved through a window from Lahore and made to stand for hours, until fellow passengers recognize him.

chapters.situation: Indentured emigration has just been ended. Gandhi is touring India and attended the 1916 Lucknow Congress.
chapters.summary: At Lucknow a Champaran peasant, Rajkumar Shukla, begs Gandhi to see the indigo planters' tyranny, under which tenants must grow indigo on three-twentieths of their land. Gandhi has never heard of Champaran, but Shukla follows him to Cawnpore, to the ashram and to Calcutta until he agrees. In early 1917 they travel to Patna like fellow peasants. At Rajendra Prasad's house the servants do not know Gandhi and will not let him use the well or the indoor latrine. Gandhi realizes Shukla cannot guide him and he must take charge himself.

updates.gandhi: Captured by Rajkumar Shukla's persistence, he goes to Champaran in 1917. Treated as a possible untouchable by Rajendra Prasad's servants.
updates.rajkumar: Follows Gandhi from Lucknow to Cawnpore to the ashram to Calcutta until he agrees to come. Turns out to have no influence at all.
updates.brajkishore: Moves the Congress resolution on Champaran. At first Gandhi takes him for an exploitative vakil.
updates.rajendra: Away from Patna when Gandhi first arrives at his house.
updates.bhupendranath: Rajkumar Shukla waits for Gandhi at his Calcutta house.
updates.indigo: The tinkathia system: three kathas in twenty must be planted with indigo for the landlord.
updates.untouchability: Strict untouchability in Bihar: Gandhi cannot draw water from the well.
updates.champaran: Gandhi, who had never heard of it, arrives in early 1917.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has reached Patna with Rajkumar Shukla, who cannot guide him, to investigate the indigo system.
chapters.summary: Mazharul Haq sends Gandhi on to Muzaffarpur, where Professor J. B. Kripalani meets him at midnight with students. Local vakils invite him, and Brajkishore Prasad and Rajendra Prasad arrive. Brajkishore impresses him this time with his humility. Gandhi is staggered by the lawyers' huge fees and concludes the courts cannot help terrified peasants; what they need is freedom from fear. He asks the vakils to serve without pay as clerks and interpreters and to be ready for jail, and they agree.

updates.gandhi: Decides Champaran needs freedom from fear, not lawsuits, and that the work may take two years.
updates.mazharul: Offers hospitality and sends Gandhi to Muzaffarpur.
updates.kripalani: Has just resigned his professorship. Meets Gandhi at midnight with students and briefs him on Bihar.
updates.brajkishore: Now impresses Gandhi with humility and faith. Organizes the vakils to work as unpaid clerks.
updates.rajkumar: His story is confirmed by local vakils.
updates.indigo: Lawyers charge four-figure fees but bring the tenants little relief.
updates.law: 'Where the ryots are so crushed and fear-stricken, law courts are useless.'

chapters.situation: Gandhi has gathered a team of Bihari vakils in Muzaffarpur and plans to investigate the peasants' grievances in Champaran.
chapters.summary: The planters' secretary calls Gandhi an outsider and the Commissioner tells him to leave. Heading by elephant to see an ill-treated tenant, Gandhi is served with an order to leave Champaran. He writes that he will not comply and is summoned for trial. He spends the night giving instructions to Brajkishore. Huge crowds gather at Motihari. Gandhi is courteous to the officials, who end up asking for his help with the crowds. Keeping the Congress name out of it, he meets the peasants and feels 'face to face with God, Ahimsa and Truth'.

updates.gandhi: Defies an order to leave Champaran. Meeting the peasants is 'a red-letter day' when he feels face to face with God, ahimsa and truth.
updates.brajkishore: Gets Gandhi's overnight instructions in case of arrest.
updates.rajkumar: Wants Gandhi to see the poorest tenants near Bettiah, his home area.
updates.champaran: Motihari overflows with peasants who have lost their fear of punishment.
updates.civildisobedience: Gandhi refuses to obey the order while staying courteous to the officials.
updates.incongress: Gandhi keeps the Congress name out of it: 'work and not name, substance and not shadow'.
updates.ahimsa: Gandhi finds his only title to the peasants' trust is his love for them, the expression of his faith in ahimsa.

status.gandhi: On trial in Motihari for defying the order

chapters.situation: Gandhi has refused an order to leave Champaran and faces trial in Motihari, with peasants thronging the court.
chapters.summary: Gandhi pleads guilty and reads a statement: he disobeyed not from disrespect for authority but in obedience to 'the higher law of our being, the voice of conscience', and accepts the penalty. Before sentencing, the Lieutenant Governor withdraws the case and the Collector offers full cooperation. It is India's first direct lesson in civil disobedience. Gandhi keeps reporters and outside leaders away to avoid giving the struggle a political colour, while planters spread lies about him and Brajkishore.

updates.gandhi: Pleads guilty; the case is withdrawn and he is free to investigate. Keeps the campaign non-political.
updates.brajkishore: Maligned by the planters, which only raises his standing with the people.
updates.malaviya: Offers to come whenever needed; Gandhi does not call him, to avoid giving the campaign a political colour.
updates.civildisobedience: India's first object lesson: disobey openly, plead guilty, and accept the penalty in obedience to conscience.
updates.champaran: The government withdraws the case and promises cooperation.
updates.indigo: Planters run a poisonous press campaign against Gandhi.

status.gandhi: Free to conduct the Champaran inquiry

chapters.situation: The case against Gandhi has been dropped and he is free to inquire into the indigo system.
chapters.summary: Gandhi refuses money from the peasants and from Bombay to avoid any all-India political colour, raising funds from Biharis and Dr. Mehta; the whole inquiry costs under Rs. 3,000. The vakils give up their servants and separate kitchens for one shared vegetarian kitchen. Volunteers cross-examine every peasant and reject unreliable statements. Police (C.I.D.) officers sit in, which makes the peasants braver and curbs exaggeration. Gandhi also meets and writes to the planters accused.

updates.gandhi: Runs the Champaran inquiry on under Rs. 3,000 with rigorous cross-examination, and courts the planters.
updates.brajkishore: Finds the team a house in fearful Motihari and helps raise funds.
updates.pjmehta: Stands ready to fund the inquiry.
updates.champaran: Crowds of peasants come to give statements, and Gandhi has to give darshan at set hours.
updates.truth: Each peasant's statement is cross-examined; unconvincing ones are rejected.
updates.simplicity: The vakils give up their servants for one shared vegetarian kitchen.

chapters.situation: The Champaran inquiry is in full swing, with thousands of peasants giving statements.
chapters.summary: Brajkishore and Rajendra Prasad lead a band of Bihari vakils. Kripalani, a Sindhi who seems more Bihari than the Biharis, guards Gandhi from darshan-seekers with humour. Seeing the peasants' ignorance, Gandhi opens primary schools in six villages, with villagers supplying food and volunteers teaching. Avantikabai Gokhale, Mahadev Desai and Narahari Parikh with their wives, Devdas and Kasturba come. The women teach cleanliness and manners more than letters, and Dr. Dev leads the sanitation work. No one is to touch politics.

updates.gandhi: Starts village schools and sanitation work in Champaran.
updates.brajkishore: One of the 'matchless pair' leading the Champaran workers.
updates.rajendra: One of the 'matchless pair' without whom Gandhi can take no step.
updates.kripalani: Gandhi's 'gatekeeper in chief', who keeps off darshan-seekers.
updates.mazharul: Visits once or twice a month, still living in pomp and splendour.
updates.desai: Mahadev Desai and his wife Durga join Gandhi in Champaran, the start of his lifelong service as Gandhi's secretary.
updates.narahari: Joins with his wife Manibehn to teach in Champaran.
updates.avantikabai: Her school becomes a model one.
updates.soman: Comes to Champaran as a volunteer teacher.
updates.devdas: Sent from the Ashram to teach in Champaran.
updates.kasturba: Summoned to teach in Champaran, though she cannot read; she teaches cleanliness and good manners.
updates.dev: Leads the medical and sanitation work for six months.
updates.education: Village schools teach cleanliness and manners, with villagers feeding the teachers.
updates.sanitation: Villages are filthy and people suffer from skin diseases.

chapters.situation: Volunteers have opened village schools in Champaran and are trying to reach the villagers' daily lives.
chapters.summary: Each school has a man and a woman volunteer, and medicine is limited to castor oil, quinine and sulphur ointment, with Dr. Dev visiting weekly. Volunteers sweep roads, clean wells and coax villagers into sanitation. A woman tells Kasturba she cannot wash her sari because it is her only one. When planters' men burn the bamboo school at Bhitiharva, Soman and Kasturba build a brick one. The work is not made permanent, because volunteers are temporary and Gandhi is called away.

updates.gandhi: Sees the depth of rural poverty, such as a woman with only one sari. His constructive work in Champaran does not last.
updates.kasturba: Runs the Bhitiharva school with Soman and rebuilds it in brick after it is burned. Hears a woman say she owns only one sari.
updates.soman: Builds a brick schoolhouse at Bhitiharva after the bamboo one is burned.
updates.dev: Supervises simple medical relief and sanitation.
updates.champaran: A school is burned, probably by planters' men.
updates.sanitation: Volunteers clean roads, wells and courtyards; some villagers refuse to join in.
updates.education: The village schools fade once the temporary volunteers leave.

chapters.situation: Thousands of peasants' statements have been recorded, and the planters are pressing the government to stop Gandhi.
chapters.summary: The Bihar government politely suggests Gandhi end his inquiry and leave. He refuses until the peasants get relief or an official inquiry is held. The Lieutenant Governor, Sir Edward Gait, appoints a committee with Gandhi as a member, accepting his conditions that he remain the peasants' advocate. The committee finds for the peasants and recommends refunds and abolition of tinkathia. With Gait's firmness the Agrarian Act passes, ending a century-old system and 'the planters' raj'.

updates.gandhi: Serves on the official inquiry committee while remaining the peasants' advocate; the century-old tinkathia system is abolished.
updates.gait: Appoints the inquiry, accepts Gandhi's conditions, and firmly carries the Agrarian Act through against the planters.
updates.indigo: Tinkathia is abolished by law and planters must refund part of their unlawful exactions, which ends 'the planters' raj'.
updates.champaran: The peasants' fear is broken and 'the stain of indigo' washed out.

chapters.situation: The tinkathia system has been abolished. Gandhi is finishing his work on the Champaran committee.
chapters.summary: Letters arrive about crop failure in Kheda and low wages for Ahmedabad's mill-workers. Gandhi goes to Ahmedabad, and his Champaran schools and cow-protection plans lapse. The labour organizer Anasuyabai is fighting her own brother, the mill-owner Ambalal Sarabhai. When the owners refuse arbitration, Gandhi advises a strike on four conditions: no violence, no molesting strikebreakers, no living on charity, and earning bread by other work while staying firm. Daily meetings under a tree and processions under the banner 'Ek Tek' (keep the pledge) follow, and he comes to know Vallabhbhai Patel. The strike lasts 21 days.

updates.gandhi: Leaves Champaran for Ahmedabad's mill strike and Kheda's crop failure; his Champaran schools close one by one.
updates.anasuyabai: Leads the mill-workers against her own brother.
updates.ambalal: Leads the mill-owners and refuses arbitration, though he is friendly with Gandhi.
updates.vallabhbhai: Gandhi comes to know him intimately during the strike.
updates.shankarlal: Gandhi comes to know him during the strike.
updates.millstrike: Ahmedabad mill workers strike under Gandhi's four conditions, with daily meetings by the Sabarmati and the banner 'Ek Tek'.
updates.kheda: Crops have failed and the peasants cannot pay the land assessment.
updates.cowprotection: Gandhi defines it as cattle-breeding, better stock, humane treatment of bullocks and model dairies. The Bettiah plan is never realized.
updates.champaran: The constructive work lapses after Gandhi leaves.
